name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,835

entries.clue: Old man put something intoxicating in magnificent joint (6)

blocks.note: pa is the familiar name for a father, the old man of the house
to lace a drink is to slip spirits into it without saying so

annotation.surface: Someone's father spiking a drink at a smart venue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint' is slang for a place in the surface and in the definition alike, so the seam between the two halves barely shows. The intoxicating stuff goes into a drink, not into the building.
annotation.definitionFit: A palace is a grand residence, and 'joint' is the slang word for any establishment, so a magnificent one is a palace.

entries.clue: Feeling under pressure to get ducks in a row (4)

indicatorNotes.under: In a down entry whatever is under something is written below it, so the feeling goes beneath the pressure rather than in front of it.

blocks.note: p is the symbol for pressure in a physics formula
an air is the manner or feeling a person gives off

annotation.surface: Somebody stressed by a deadline trying to get organised.
annotation.walkthrough: The idiom 'get your ducks in a row' does all the misleading. These ducks are cricket's: a batter dismissed without scoring is out for a duck, and the clue wants two of them.
annotation.definitionFit: In cricket a batter out for nought scores a duck, and a pair is the name for two of them, one in each innings of the same match.

entries.clue: A bit of Latin, Greek and English in grid (7)

indicatorNotes.A bit of: A bit of a word is a piece of it, and the smallest piece a setter can mean is the letter it starts with.

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
Attic is the Greek of ancient Athens, the dialect of Plato and the tragedians
e is the standard abbreviation for English

annotation.surface: Three languages turning up together in one grid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A bit of Latin' looks as though it wants the abbreviation LAT, and it is one letter only. ATTIC for Greek is the piece worth keeping: the Athenian dialect standing in for the language itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A lattice is the criss-crossed framework of strips you get in a garden trellis or across a pie, which is a grid.

entries.clue: Being round climbers with fruit, dog on sierra gets to eat (9)

indicatorNotes.gets to eat: Whatever gets to eat closes over its meal, so the letters doing the eating take the other word inside them.

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel, the crossword's standard dog
vines climb, and the fruit they carry is grapes
sierra is S in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A dog on a mountainside getting at the fruit on the climbing plants.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sierra' is the NATO alphabet's S rather than the mountain range the surface paints. 'Being round' is a noun phrase naming a quality, not a description of where anyone is standing.
annotation.definitionFit: Curviness is the state of being round rather than straight, the quality a curved thing has.

entries.clue: Elaborate on principle of vegetarianism? (5,3)

annotation.definitionNote: The second half is not a synonym but the answer read as a slogan, so it names a principle where the first names an action.

blocks.note: to add detail and substance to something that is only an outline so far
read as two words giving a ruling about meat, the one rule every vegetarian keeps

annotation.surface: An examiner asking you to expand on the principle behind vegetarianism.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark is the only signal, and it turns a request into a slogan. Flesh is what meat is called at the butcher's, and the vegetarian's position on it is the second reading.
annotation.definitionFit: To flesh out a plan is to put substance on its bones; read as an order about meat, it is the vegetarian's one rule.

entries.clue: Comfort on the way out, girl boxes stock (4,5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Comfort' is a mass noun and the answer is plural: the several rites together make up the one comfort offered, so the setter counts them as a single service.

indicatorNotes.boxes: To box a thing is to shut it in a container, so the girl's letters close around what follows.

blocks.note: lass is the northern and Scottish word for a girl
a stock phrase or a stock character is a worn, trite one

annotation.surface: A girl on her last day at work boxing up the shop's stock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the way out' stops meaning leaving a job the moment you notice the comfort is a priest's. 'Stock' is the adjective of stock characters, not goods on a shelf.
annotation.definitionFit: The last rites are the prayers and anointing a priest gives someone who is dying, the church's comfort at the end.

entries.clue: Alexander, band leader in alley? (5)

indicatorNotes.leader in: The leader in a word is the letter at its head, the one that goes first.

blocks.note: a sash is the band of cloth worn over one shoulder or round the waist
its opening letter

annotation.surface: A bandleader called Alexander playing down a back alley.
annotation.walkthrough: Alexander sets up 'band leader' as a job — Alexander's Ragtime Band is right there in the ear — when the two words belong to different pieces of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Sasha is the Russian pet form of Alexander, the everyday name an Aleksandr goes by, so the question mark flags one example of the name.

entries.clue: Opportunity to write home during journey back (7)

indicatorNotes.during: What happens during something happens inside it, so these letters are planted in the middle of the other word.
indicatorNotes.back: Back means written the other way round, so that word's letters are set down from its end.

blocks.note: a go is a stint or a turn at something, which is how it loosely covers a journey; here it is written from the end
to pen a letter is to write it
someone who is in is at home

annotation.surface: Finding a moment to write home in the middle of the trip back.
annotation.walkthrough: Everything here reads as travel arrangements, and the definition is the single word at the front. 'Home' for IN is the sense of the darts caller and the phone message: in, and therefore at home.
annotation.definitionFit: An opening is a gap in a diary or a market that lets you get started — the chance itself, not the hole in a wall.

entries.clue: Cast heard Othello upset audience there for Lear? (6,4)

indicatorNotes.heard: What is heard reaches you as a noise, so you write down a spelling of the sound rather than the word itself.
indicatorNotes.upset: In a down entry an upset word is tipped over and climbs back up the column, so its letters run the other way.

blocks.note: something cast has been thrown, and that past participle said aloud is spelt another way
Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice, and the word is tipped over

annotation.surface: A company performing Othello upsetting the people who had come for King Lear.
annotation.walkthrough: Two Shakespeare tragedies in one sentence, and the answer belongs to neither: 'audience' here is the formal reception a monarch grants, not the people in the seats.
annotation.definitionFit: A throne room is where a monarch sits to receive people, so it is where a king like Lear grants an audience.

entries.clue: Very thin person beginning to ask whether to put weight on (4)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: A word's beginning is the letter it starts with and nothing more.
indicatorNotes.on: In a down entry something put on another thing sits above it, so the weight goes to the top.

blocks.note: w is the abbreviation for weight on a chart or in a formula
its opening letter
if does the job of whether — tell me if you are coming

annotation.surface: A very thin person starting to wonder about gaining a few pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: The sentence is one continuous thought about a thin person, so nothing marks where the definition stops and the instructions start. In a down clue, putting weight 'on' puts it at the top of the column.
annotation.definitionFit: A waif is a stray, neglected child, and the word is used of anyone who looks unusually thin and frail.

entries.clue: Spaces between latrines changed to accommodate volume (9)

indicatorNotes.changed: Letters that have been changed do not stay in the order they were given.
indicatorNotes.to accommodate: To accommodate is to find room for a guest, so the shuffled letters take the extra one in among them.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters
v is the standard abbreviation for volume

annotation.surface: The gaps between army latrines being altered to make room for more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Latrines changed' reads as building work rather than as an instruction, which is the whole disguise. Strictly it is the latrines that are shuffled and the volume they then take in — the same nine letters either way.
annotation.definitionFit: Intervals are the gaps left between things, whether in time or across a floor.

entries.clue: Take fleece off husband wearing brand (5)

indicatorNotes.wearing: Somebody wearing a garment is inside it, so this letter goes within the word that follows.

blocks.note: to sear is to burn a mark on, which is what branding a beast does
h is the standard abbreviation for husband on a form

annotation.surface: Pulling a fleece jacket off a man dressed in a designer label.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' is the coat on a sheep rather than the zip-up jacket, and 'brand' is the hot iron rather than the label — the surface borrows both words back from the high street.
annotation.definitionFit: To shear a sheep is to clip its fleece off, the yearly job that takes the wool away.

entries.clue: Intentionally false leads detective inspectors lined up? (14)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Leads' is plural where the answer is a mass noun, allowed because the several planted trails are all the one stuff.

blocks.note: DI is the police rank of detective inspector, and more than one of them takes an s
troops lined up for parade are in formation

annotation.surface: False trails sending a line of detective inspectors off in the wrong direction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leads' looks like the verb driving the sentence along and is the last word of the definition instead. The question mark is there to cover the parade-ground whimsy of the second half.
annotation.definitionFit: Disinformation is false material put about on purpose to mislead — precisely the sort of lead that is planted rather than found.

entries.clue: Really worry about case of neighing chanteuse (10)

indicatorNotes.about: Letters set about something go round it, so the pair just clued opens up to hold what follows.
indicatorNotes.case of: A word's case is its outside, the letters at either end with everything between them shut in.

blocks.note: so does the work of really — she was so tired
the first and last letters of the word
to stress about something is to worry about it

annotation.surface: A singer seriously worried about a bout of neighing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chanteuse' is French for a woman who sings and stands alone at the end as the definition. 'Case' is the box sense of the word, not a case of anything medical.
annotation.definitionFit: A songstress is a woman who sings, which is what the French chanteuse names — the cabaret or nightclub singer.

entries.clue: Too nice to dismiss minister, on reflection, during October (9)

indicatorNotes.on reflection: A thing seen on reflection comes back mirrored, so those letters are written the other way round.
indicatorNotes.during: What happens during something happens inside it, so this chunk is planted in the middle of the month.

blocks.note: oct is the calendar's short form for the month
to axe somebody is to dismiss them from a job
a minister of religion is a Reverend, shortened to Rev on the envelope

annotation.surface: A boss who, thinking again, is too kind to sack the minister in October.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nice' in its older sense means precise — a nice distinction — and that is the sense wanted; the kindly reading belongs to the surface. 'On reflection' looks like second thoughts and is an instruction to turn letters round.
annotation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense is precise, so something overexact is too nice — fussier about detail than it needs to be.

entries.clue: Unreadable novel? (9)

blocks.note: read as so badly written that nobody can get through it, and meant as offering nothing on a page to read at all
the work of fiction itself, which reaches this particular customer as sound rather than as print

annotation.surface: A novel so badly written that nobody can get through it.
annotation.walkthrough: Two words with no letters to take apart: the joke is that the thing truly cannot be read, because it is not printed. Somebody does read it, of course — aloud, into a microphone.
annotation.definitionFit: An audiobook is a novel recorded for listening, so there is no text in front of you to read — unreadable in the most literal way.

entries.clue: On break, flipping thing calling you back to work (5)

annotation.definition: thing calling you back to work

indicatorNotes.flipping: To flip a thing is to turn it right over, so the letters just assembled are read from the end instead.

blocks.note: re means on the subject of, as at the head of a memo
a break in a hedge or in a timetable is a gap

annotation.surface: Someone on a break, irritated by the flipping thing that summons them back to work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as the mild swear-word aimed at the device, and that is its disguise: it is the instruction. 'On' for RE is the memo-heading sense, a note on a subject.
annotation.definitionFit: A pager is the little bleeper a doctor or an on-call engineer carries, whose one job is to summon them back to work.

entries.clue: Macron's ready with team name in his office (9)

indicatorNotes.in: What is in a word sits inside it, so these letters are dropped into the middle of the French one.

blocks.note: Macron is French, and prêt is the French for ready
a side is a team — the side that plays on Saturday
n is the standard abbreviation for name on a form

annotation.surface: Macron waiting in his office with a team's name to hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Macron's ready' asks for a French word rather than an English one — the possessive marks whose language is wanted. 'The ready' is also slang for cash, which is the other trap the phrase sets.
annotation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Macron is the French head of state, and the office he holds is that of president.

entries.clue: Biologist's type of knee (5)

annotation.definitionNote: The second definition is Latin rather than English: it translates a case ending, so it defines a word-form instead of offering a synonym.

blocks.note: the rank in the classification table that sits just above species, shared by creatures near enough to be close relatives
read as a kind of knee, and meant as Latin: the anatomist's word for the joint, put into the case that means 'of'

annotation.surface: A biologist describing a particular kind of knee.
annotation.walkthrough: The five words read as a single phrase and break after 'type', with nothing marking the join. Latin nouns change their ending to mean 'of', and that ending is the whole of the second half.
annotation.definitionFit: In taxonomy a genus is the rank grouping related species, and genus is also the Latin genitive of genu, the knee — hence 'of knee'.

entries.clue: Broad area of new floor sunken in the middle (7)

indicatorNotes.new: Something made new has been made over, and letters made over do not keep the order they arrived in.
indicatorNotes.in the middle: The middle of a word is the letters at its centre, with the same number dropped from each end.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, five letters
the two letters at the centre of the word, two having gone from each side

annotation.surface: A wide stretch of new flooring that has sagged in the middle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broad area' is not about size: the Broads are the lakes and waterways of an English county, and the county is what is wanted. 'New' reads as a description of the floor and is the instruction to shuffle it.
annotation.definitionFit: Norfolk is the eastern English county whose Broads — a network of shallow lakes and slow rivers — make it the Broad area.

entries.clue: Outlaw maybe does bother to carry unloaded pistols around (9)

indicatorNotes.to carry: To carry something is to hold it inside you, so the letters doing the carrying close around what they are given.
indicatorNotes.unloaded: An unloaded weapon has had its contents taken out, so the word keeps only the letters at its two ends.
indicatorNotes.around: Something brought around has been turned about, so those two letters are set down the other way.

blocks.note: does are female deer, so more than one doe is deer
much ado about nothing — ado is fuss or bother
the outer letters of the word, left when everything loaded between them comes out

annotation.surface: An outlaw who can be bothered to cart a pair of empty pistols about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb propping the sentence up and is the plural of doe. 'Unloaded' does to the word exactly what it claims to do to the guns: empties the middle out.
annotation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw of the old American West, the sort with nothing left to lose — one example of the breed.

entries.clue: Painter and writer introduced to people who try not to drink coffee (7)

indicatorNotes.introduced to: People introduced to a group are taken in among them, so the letters just clued go inside the ones that follow.

blocks.clueFragment: people who try not to drink
blocks.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members are off the drink
an RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's standard painter
Bic is the French firm whose disposable ballpoint is the everyday pen

annotation.surface: An artist and an author being introduced to people trying to give up coffee.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word, and the surface hides it by reading 'try not to drink coffee' as one phrase. The drink those people are actually off is something stronger.
annotation.definitionFit: Arabica is the species most of the world's coffee is grown from, so it names the drink by its bean.

entries.clue: Jargony long article IMO needs editing (14)

indicatorNotes.needs editing: Text that needs editing has to have its parts moved about, so these letters will not stay as they are.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, fourteen letters

annotation.surface: A reader complaining that a wordy online piece could do with a trim.
annotation.walkthrough: IMO is the internet's shorthand for 'in my opinion', dropped in so that it reads as a commenter hedging rather than as three more letters of fodder. Everything after the first word is shuffled.
annotation.definitionFit: Terminological means having to do with technical terms, the specialist vocabulary of a trade, which is what calling a piece of writing jargony says of it.

entries.clue: Which organ is filled with Zeus's blood? (5)

indicatorNotes.is filled with: Whatever is filled with a thing has it inside, so the words before this hold the letters within them.

blocks.note: the letters run straight on across the space between the two words

annotation.surface: A quiz question asking which organ holds the blood of Zeus.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is a whole question, which is how the letters pass unnoticed inside it. The Olympian gods were held to have this stuff in their veins in place of blood.
annotation.definitionFit: Ichor is the fluid the Greeks said ran in the veins of their gods instead of blood, Zeus's among them.

entries.clue: Get rid of square unfashionable clothes (4)

indicatorNotes.clothes: To clothe a thing is to put a covering round it, so the word just clued wraps the letter beside it.

blocks.note: what is out is no longer in fashion
s is the abbreviation for square in an address or on a map

annotation.surface: Throwing away some hopelessly unfashionable clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as the noun and works as the verb, so the sentence seems to be about dowdy garments. 'Square' has meant unfashionable since the jazz age, which is why the words sit so comfortably together.
annotation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to drive them out of a post or a place, which is getting rid of them.

entries.clue: You might say faded, not really blonde? (4)

indicatorNotes.You might say: What you might say is the noise a word makes, so you write down a different spelling of that same noise.

blocks.note: a colour that has faded has died away, and that word said aloud is spelt another way

annotation.surface: Someone doubting that a washed-out blonde is the real thing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Faded' is a sound to copy, not a report on the state of the hair, though the surface makes the two look like the same complaint. The question mark carries the whole joke about roots.
annotation.definitionFit: Hair that is dyed has had its colour out of a bottle, so a dyed blonde is not really blonde at all.

entries.clue: Big date, record ejaculation from Scot (5)

blocks.note: an EP is the extended-play record, longer than a single and shorter than an album
och is the Scottish exclamation — och aye

annotation.surface: A Scot exclaiming over a record on a big anniversary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ejaculation' is the old word for a sudden cry, the sense the King James Bible uses, and it is what makes the surface read so oddly. Nothing joins the two pieces but a comma.
annotation.definitionFit: An epoch is the date an age is reckoned from, the point at which a new era starts, so it is a big date indeed.

entries.clue: Dirt spread by insect on doughnut (9)

indicatorNotes.spread: Letters spread about have been scattered out of the order they came in.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters — 'by' is part of the material, not the agent it pretends to be
a doughnut is a ring, so it stands for the round letter

annotation.surface: Muck carried onto a doughnut by a fly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spread by insect' reads as how the dirt travels, so 'by' passes for grammar when it is really two letters of the material. 'Dirt' is the smutty sense, the kind a censor cuts.
annotation.definitionFit: Dirt is what people call talk or material that is indecent, and an obscenity is a single piece of exactly that.

entries.clue: Helicopter Republican agreed is turning blue (8)

indicatorNotes.turning: A turning word comes out the other way round, its letters read from the end.

blocks.note: the party's initial, the two letters that mean agreed and the word 'is', all three written out backwards
the sky is the blue overhead, and sky blue is named after it

annotation.surface: A Republican conceding that the political map is turning blue.
annotation.walkthrough: Blue is the other party's colour in American politics, which is what gives the surface its sting. 'Is' looks like the verb holding the sentence together and hands over two letters of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Igor Sikorsky's firm built the first mass-produced helicopters, so a Sikorsky is a helicopter named after its maker.

entries.clue: Coming soon from Jonathan Demme ... (2,4)

indicatorNotes.from: Letters taken from something are a piece of it, sitting unbroken inside the words named.

blocks.note: the letters run on without a break across the space between the two names

annotation.surface: A trailer promising a new film from the director.
annotation.walkthrough: Jonathan Demme directed The Silence of the Lambs, and a name at the end of a trailer is the last place anyone hunts for letters. The trailing dots are part of the pose.
annotation.definitionFit: Something at hand is close by in time as well as in place — near enough to be about to happen.
